# The build tag for a GOFIPS140 snapshot must be set, and the purego tag
# rejected, when -tags is used with 'go install pkg@version' or
# 'go run pkg@version'. Toolchain selection resolves pkg@version, and so
# initializes the FIPS settings, before the -tags flag is parsed.
# Verifies golang.org/issue/83334.

env GOFIPS140=v1.0.0

# Go+BoringCrypto conflicts with GOFIPS140.
[GOEXPERIMENT:boringcrypto] skip

# -tags on the command line keeps the snapshot's build tag
go install -tags=foo example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
go version -m $GOPATH/bin/a$GOEXE
stdout '^\tbuild\t-tags=foo,fips140v1\.0$'
rm $GOPATH/bin

# so does -tags in GOFLAGS
env GOFLAGS=-tags=foo
go install example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
go version -m $GOPATH/bin/a$GOEXE
stdout '^\tbuild\t-tags=foo,fips140v1\.0$'
env GOFLAGS=

# the purego tag is still rejected
! go install -tags=purego example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
stderr '^go: cannot use GOFIPS140 with the purego build tag$'
! go run -tags=purego example.com/cmd/a@v1.0.0
stderr '^go: cannot use GOFIPS140 with the purego build tag$'
